what_it_does: Recommendation systems (the kind used by e-commerce and streaming platforms) often find relevant items by computing a similarity score between a query vector and millions of stored embedding vectors (dense lists of numbers that represent items). This is done as a sparse matrix-vector multiply (SpMV — multiplying a vector against a large matrix where most entries are zero) to find the top-K most similar matches, but scanning the full high-precision matrix is slow because irregular memory access patterns waste bandwidth. AccelES splits the work into two stages: first it scans a compressed, lower-precision (fewer bits per number) version of the matrix to quickly narrow down candidates, then it does full-precision scoring only on that smaller shortlist. Two new data layouts for the sparse matrix — called Ultra-CSR and Random-CSR — are designed to make memory accesses for irregular sparsity patterns more efficient. The net effect is faster top-K retrieval with less data read from memory.
